title: Concerto-style scores for symphony orchestras
summary: A Binghamton friend wrote scores featuring the bass; Stewart performed with the Binghamton and Indianapolis symphonies.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: Oh. So now when did you begin to encounter classical bassists who were interested in what you were doing?

Well, I would say that I didn't exactly encounter any classical bassists, but how it happened was that -- well, let's start off like this. I had a friend of mine right here in Binghamton write a few scores for me to play with symphonic orchestras and they were written so that I could be the feature all through performing with the symphonic orchestra. Let's say the Indianapolis Symphony, who I performed with. There was a bass player whom I met who played with the Indianapolis Symphony. We became friends. I don't exactly remember his name, but the thing was --
It wasn't Barry Green, was it?
Barry Green? Was it Barry Green?
I'm trying to remember Barry Green -- I think Barry Green was with the -- I'm not sure. Barry Green was with one of those Midwest Symphonies. I thought it might have been --
Anyway, these arrangements were made for me featuring, you know, the bass throughout --
A concerto for string bass and orchestra.

That's right, sure. And that's how I have come about to perform with two, the Binghamton Symphony and the Indianapolis Symphony. And it's being worked on for me to play more symphonies as time goes by.
